headline: Test 2: Virginia, 1640–1705 · 44:19

items.title: 44:19 · Out of the first five thousand indentured
items.detail: Out of the first five thousand indentured servants brought into Virginia, only 241 survived their terms and acquired land of their own.

items.title: 44:28 · Because poor European servants and African laborers
items.detail: Because poor European servants and African laborers experienced the same whip, the same tobacco fields, and the same planter oligarchy, their class interests aligned naturally at the bottom of the colony.

items.title: 44:40 · They fraternized in the quarters formed cross-racial
items.detail: They fraternized in the quarters, formed cross-racial families, shared food, and escaped together into the frontier.

items.title: 44:46 · Even a century later George Washington placed
items.detail: Even a century later, George Washington placed runaway advertisements in the Maryland Gazette and the Virginia Gazette offering identical cash rewards for the recapture of escaped white indentured servants and escaped enslaved Black laborers.

items.title: 45:00 · To break that natural solidarity among field
items.detail: To break that natural solidarity among field laborers, the Virginia planter Elite executed an iterative sixty-five-year compilation of racial law between 1640 and 1705.
